Powerful Earthquake Disrupts Industry and Transport Across Mexico

MEXICO CITY, June 18 — A powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck central Mexico on Tuesday, causing widespread disruption to industrial operations and transport infrastructure across the country, authorities said. The quake, which struck at 9:12 a.m. local time with an epicenter near Puebla, was felt as far north as Monterrey and as far south as Oaxaca.

Initial reports indicate that several major manufacturing hubs suspended operations following power outages and structural assessments. Grupo Simec SAB de CV, a leading producer in the steel sector, confirmed that it had temporarily halted production at its main plant in Tlaxcala as engineers inspect facilities for damage. “Our immediate priority is the safety of our workforce and the integrity of our operations,” the company said in a statement.

The National Chamber of Manufacturing Industries said at least 40 industrial parks reported disruptions ranging from machinery failures to damaged warehouses. “It’s too early to estimate the total impact, but we are seeing significant interruptions across automotive, steel, and electronics clusters,” said chamber president Eduardo Salinas.

Mexico’s federal highway agency reported partial closures on key freight corridors due to collapsed overpasses and landslides, slowing the delivery of goods to ports and border crossings. The peso fell 1.7% against the dollar in midday trading.

Emergency services are still assessing full damage as aftershocks continue. President Andrés Manuel López Obrador urged calm and promised federal support for communities and businesses affected. “We are mobilizing all available resources for rescue and recovery,” he said in a televised address.
